fields.title: «Polka»: a quarter for a rewrite
fields.summary: Tech lead asks for a quarter to rewrite the catalog, roadmap demands five features.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do in the next two quarters? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. The tech lead asks for a quarter to rewrite the catalog service: «the current implementation won't survive growth, every feature is hard». At the same time, the roadmap team insists on five features this quarter.
fields.brief/objective: Deliver five features and pay down debt, spending less calendar time, not more.
fields.brief/constraints: Buying an engine costs 180 thousand per month and vendor lock-in.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you do in the next two quarters and calculate.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Technical debt is measured in weeks, not opinions
fields.learnTakeaway/body: The dispute of «features first or debt first» is resolved by two estimates of the same scope: with debt and without it. The difference is the overpayment, and if it exceeds the cost of cleanup, the case is closed. Next comes calendar bargaining: buying sometimes eliminates both the most expensive feature and part of the debt immediately, but brings a recurring payment and dependency that must also be named as a number.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Favorites (8 wks), price comparison (6 wks), product recommendations (5 wks), category reports (4 wks), facet filters (7 wks). All five are in the catalog domain.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: The same five: 3, 2, 3, 2, 4 weeks. Total 14 vs 30.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Over half a year, 12 incidents, 4 related to the catalog.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Quarter for rewrite, then features. 12 + 14 = 26 weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: longer on the calendar, but cleaner. Two quarters without product results in the catalog is hard to explain.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Features as is, debt later. 30 weeks for five features.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: results flow continuously. 16 weeks overpayment, and debt continues to grow. Performance problems under growth are not solved.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Rewrite plus buying a search and filter engine
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: 12 weeks of rewrite minus what the engine covers, plus 3 weeks of integration.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: filters (7 wks) are covered by the engine in 3 weeks, rewrite is shortened. 180k/mo ongoing. The remaining four features after—10 weeks without debt. *Total approx 3 + 9 + 10 = 22 weeks and all five features.*
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Partial cleanup: only what blocks the five features
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Partial cleanup: only what blocks the five features. 6 weeks instead of 12.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: overpayment is partially reduced, say to 6 weeks instead of 16. Total 6 + 20 = 26 weeks. Structural performance problem under growth remains.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not convert debt into plan overpayment
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not calculate total purchase cost
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Cost of the request and recurring payment is not weighed against team effort
